newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.02 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.02 percent Thursday to close at 1.0626 per dollar on inflows of the U.S. currency in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $30 million surplus on Thursday. On Wednesday, forex contracts posted a $84.8 million surplus.

The market is divided about the timing of the next decline in the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said. Some players believe the central bank could lower the mini-band again in coming days. Others think it will hold steady until April 30.
The central bank last lowered the mini-band on Tuesday to between 1.0625 and 1.0675 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.52 percent against the dollar compared with an average drop of between 0.5 percent and 0.6 percent in the past three months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.02 percent to end at 1.0676 per dollar.
In the parallel market, the real fell 0.44 percent to close at 1.135 per dollar, traders said.
